proof.criterion: R1. An applied stack that sets nothing new sends nothing new: the schema requires nothing new and clusterOnly carries no default.
proof.surface: The served schema read from the plugin binary built at this head by the real Pulumi CLI, as a consumer's pulumi package get-schema reads it.
proof.command: pulumi package get-schema $TMPDIR/infra774-tester/pulumi-resource-envoy-infra | jq -c '{required: .resources["envoy-infra:gcp:Dispatch"].requiredInputs, clusterOnly: .resources["envoy-infra:gcp:Dispatch"].inputProperties.clusterOnly, hasDefault: (.resources["envoy-infra:gcp:Dispatch"].inputProperties.clusterOnly | has("default")), version: .version}'
proof.observed: {"required":["region","hostname"],"clusterOnly":{"type":"boolean","plain":true},"hasDefault":false,"version":"6.0.0"} — clusterOnly is a plain, non-secret boolean outside requiredInputs with no schema default, so a stack that sets nothing sends no property for it, and the thirteen Dispatch inputs are optional in the schema while the resolver still requires them with the mode off.
proof.negativeControl: The same CLI read of the plugin built from the branch's base (version 5.4.0) prints fifteen requiredInputs — region, hostname, tailnetDnsName, tags, tailnetAuthKey, tailnetService, envoyImage, tailscaleImage, cloudSqlProxyImage, frontDoorToolsImage, natsUrl, natsSeedSecret, signInClientId, signInClientSecret and signInDomain — and inputProperties holding no clusterOnly at all, so the read tells the two schemas apart and the change to requiredInputs is exactly the thirteen inputs this issue makes optional.

notes: The refusal table is sound under inspection as well as under its own tests: the production table (gcp.dispatchClusterOnlyRefusals in dispatch.go) is driven row by row through the resolver by TestDispatchClusterOnlyRefusesEveryDispatchInput, and TestDispatchEveryInputIsLiveOrRefusedUnderClusterOnly holds the test's table equal to DispatchArgs' pulumi tags less the four live inputs, so a row that named the wrong field or an input added later cannot pass in silence.

A consumer that deliberately strips every Dispatch input and turns clusterOnly on in one change is not refused, and the component would then plan to delete the database and the Kubernetes objects. That is a deliberate act and matches the README's wording ('a stack already running Dispatch cannot turn it on: such a stack sets the inputs the mode refuses'); it is recorded here so the reviewer judges the sentence knowingly, not as a defect.
